title: Sangwol/Jogye walking pilgrimage India-Nepal
description: 108+ monastics of the ROK walking pilgrimage hosted by the Jogye Order with Sangwol Society; route Sarnath -> Shravasti via Bodh Gaya, Vulture Peak/Rajgir, Nalanda, Vaishali, Kushinagar, Lumbini, Kapilavastu; 1,167 km / 43 days (~200-strong delegation reported)
significance: Largest documented Korean monastic walking pilgrimage in India; PIB-documented
evidence: PIB press release PRID=1896682; Korea Bizwire 2023-02-10; India Narrative 2023-03-22; The Federal

title: Bexpo 2026 Buddhist exchange (IBC - Jogye lay)
description: At the Seoul International Buddhism Expo (Bexpo 2026), IBC Director General Abhijit Halder presented a Buddha statue to Jung Won-ju, president of the Lay Buddhist Association of the Jogye Order; cultural/spiritual cooperation agreed
significance: First documented IBC-Jogye lay exchange in Korea; institutional channel (INSTITUTIONAL)
evidence: Korea Herald 2026-04-09 (Sanjay Kumar); Our Buddhism World 2026-04-10

title: 2nd Global Buddhist Summit
description: Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; IBC + Ministry of Culture; theme 'Collective Wisdom, United Voice and Mutual Coexistence'; 30+ countries, 800+ attendees. Korean participation CONFIRMED: Jogye international-exchange committee member / propagation team head Munjong sunim attended as representative of 총무원장 Jinwoo, whose congratulatory message was read aloud
significance: Second edition of India's flagship Buddhist summit; Jogye Order official participation documented
evidence: Tongbulgyo News 2026-02-01; Buddhist Door Tea House 2026-01-18; IBC official event PDF; DD News 2026-01-18

title: Jungto Society annual India pilgrimage program
description: Annual pilgrimage program (35th edition early 2026 implied; 36th: 14-30 Jan 2027, 16N17D, 500 participants, registration from 2026-05-25); Bodh Gaya region
significance: Largest recurring Korean lay pilgrimage to India

title: Delhi University - BGICBS academic MOU
description: Academic exchange agreement between the University of Delhi and the Bodh Gaya International College of Buddhist Studies (BGICBS, Chancellor: Ven. Buddhavara)
significance: Formalizes the main Indian university - Korean-led Buddhist college academic channel

title: Jogye delegation pilgrimage Sarnath -> Bodh Gaya
description: Jogye Order delegation pilgrimage from Sarnath to Bodh Gaya (Mahabodhi), May 2022
significance: Precursor delegation ahead of Bunhwangsa India dedication

title: Jogye pilgrimage to the 8 great sites + Nepal
description: 13N14D Jogye Order pilgrimage to 8 great Buddhist sites + Nepal, including a visit to Yeoraesunwon (Korean-run temple at Bodh Gaya)

title: Bunhwangsa India groundbreaking
description: Groundbreaking of Bunhwangsa India, the Jogye Order's first temple in India, at Bodh Gaya; completion targeted 2022; project launched 2019-04 by the 36th administration (백만원력결집)
significance: Jogye Order's first permanent temple in India

title: Bunhwangsa India dedication (대웅보전 준공식)
description: Dedication ceremony of the main hall (대웅보전) of Bunhwangsa India; 150-person Jogye official delegation ('official first pilgrimage' - 공식대표단 첫 순례) led by 총무원장 Wonhaeng; 3 years after the 2019 vow
significance: First official Jogye Order pilgrimage delegation to India; temple completion
evidence: Hyunbul News 2022-05-19; Jogye Order news; Korea Times 2022-05-24

title: Global Buddhist Summit 2023
description: First Global Buddhist Summit, Ashok Hotel, New Delhi (IBC + Ministry of Culture); ~30 countries, 500+ Buddhist leaders; PM Modi and Culture Minister Kishan Reddy attended; themes incl. environmental crisis/sustainability and preservation of the Nalanda Buddhist tradition. Korean participation CONFIRMED: Jogye 해외특별교구 교구장 직무대행 Jeongbeom sunim attended as official representative on behalf of 총무원장
significance: First edition of India's flagship Buddhist summit; Jogye Order official participation documented
evidence: Hyunbul News 2023-04-27; IBC official event file; Drishti IAS daily news analysis

title: ICYBS 2025 (3rd Int'l Conf. of Young Buddhist Scholars)
description: Dr Ambedkar International Centre, Delhi; IBC + Ministry of Culture + Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment; theme 'Wisdom Transmission in Buddha Dhamma in the 21st Century'; 4 panels + National Museum special presentation; key figures: Jangchup Choeden Rinpoche (SG IBC), Rana Pratap Singh (VC Gautam Buddha Univ.), K.T.S. Sarao, Abhijit Halder (DG IBC), Yeshi Dawa. Official IBC report names no Korean participant; PIB attendee list (India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Vietnam, Cambodia, Russia, Taiwan) contains no Korea
significance: Young-scholars track of the GBS cycle; Korean participation NOT DOCUMENTED
evidence: IBC official event report; PIB PRID=2156138; DD India 2025-08

title: KBPF 2026 India pilgrimage (Dharamsala/Ajanta-Ellora/Sanchi)
description: 8N9D India pilgrimage organized by the Korea Buddhism Promotion Foundation (대한불교진흥원): Dharamsala, Ajanta/Ellora caves, Sanchi Stupa; Air India; fees 4.59M KRW (10+ persons) / 4.09M (15+); registration open from 2026-07-02
significance: Distinct 2026 India pilgrimage by a Korean Buddhist foundation (not Jogye Order); answers the 'distinct 2026 pilgrimage' open question

title: BBS Seon Meditation Tour 4 India-Nepal
description: 8N10D India-Nepal pilgrimage organized by BBS (Buddhist Broadcasting System): Delhi, Lucknow, Varanasi, Bodh Gaya, Rajgir, Vaishali, Kushinagar, Shravasti, Lumbini, Pokhara, Kathmandu; led by 선업 스님 (former Jogye 포교원장); 3.42M KRW
significance: Korean Buddhist broadcaster-organized pilgrimage crossing into 2026; documents the 2026 pilgrimage landscape

title: Korea-India 50th anniversary cultural exchange (Jogye + ROK Embassy)
description: Co-hosted by the Jogye Order (총무원장 Jinwoo) and the ROK Embassy in India: 21 Mar 2023 temple-food dinner (사찰음식 만찬) at ambassador Jang Jae-bok's residence (chef 정관스님; 어산종장 동환스님's 축원 화청); NGMA exhibition '부처님의 땅! 인도에서 한국문화를 만나다' (22 Mar - 30 Apr: 연등, media art, temple-stay photos); ~40 attendees incl. Apurva Chandra (Indian I&B Secretary) and Korean lawmakers; ambassador praised the Sangwol pilgrimage for strengthening bilateral ties
significance: First Jogye Order-ROK Embassy co-hosted cultural event in India; official diplomatic recognition of the Sangwol pilgrimage's value

title: Korean Buddhist delegation to India (국제불교문제연구소)
description: 6-member Korean Buddhist delegation dispatched by the International Buddhist Problems Research Institute (국제불교문제연구소) toured India's sacred sites (Dec 1981) and recently returned (reported 1982-01-19); met PM Indira Gandhi for ~30 minutes, presenting a Silla gold-crown replica and a Buddhist bell; visited Nalanda and donated a facsimile of the Haeinsa Tripitaka Koreana as research material for Korean Buddhist studies; in Sri Lanka agreed a sisterhood between Kelaniya Temple and Korea's Bongeunsa
significance: First documented institutional Korean Buddhist delegation to India in the post-war era; audience with the Indian PM; Tripitaka donation at Nalanda
evidence: Dong-A Ilbo 1982-01-19 (Naver News Library); corroborated by Hyunbul News 2023-02-27

title: Dongguk University - Nalanda University MOU
description: Academic cooperation agreement signed at Nalanda University between Dongguk University (president 윤재웅; 건학위원장 돈관 스님) and Nalanda University (Vice-Chancellor Sunaina Singh): joint education and research cooperation, plus a '순례' (pilgrimage) themed international conference and Korea-India 50th-anniversary activities
significance: First MOU between a Korean Buddhist university and the modern Nalanda University; revives the ancient Nalanda-Silla channel as contemporary institutional exchange

title: Enshrinement of Dhyānabhadra's relics at Hoeamsa
description: On King Kongmin's order (1370) a stupa enshrining the relics of the Indian master Dhyānabhadra (Jikong) was built at Hoeamsa, supervised by Naong Hyegeun - formally declaring Naong's succession of Jikong's lineage
significance: Earliest documented enshrinement of an Indian master's relics in Korea; material anchor of the Jikong lineage at the Nalanda-modeled Hoeamsa
evidence: Dongguk University Buddhist Culture Portal (KBDI0001421): 1370 stupa on Kongmin's order, Naong supervised; corroborated by Hyunbul News 2017-01-26

title: Return of Hoeamsa relics (Jikong/Naong + Buddha relics) from Boston MFA
description: Relics of Dhyānabhadra (Jikong) and Naong, enshrined with Buddha relics (Shakyamuni, Kashyapa, Dipankara) that Jikong brought from India, were returned to Korea from the Boston Museum of Fine Arts (illegally removed during the colonial era; acquired by the MFA 1939; return agreed 2023-24): delivered 2024-04-16, arrived in Korea 04-18, relocation rite at Jogye's Buddhist History & Culture Memorial Hall 04-19, re-enshrined at Hoeamsa 2024-05-19
significance: Modern completion of the 14th-century relic legacy: relics of Indian provenance (Buddha's relics carried from India by the Indian master Jikong) physically returned to the temple he founded

title: Wang ocheonchukguk jeon first public display at National Museum of Korea
description: The BnF's Dunhuang manuscript of Hyecho's Wang ocheonchukguk jeon (往五天竺國傳) - the sole surviving 8th-century record of India by a Silla monk - was loaned to the National Museum of Korea for the '실크로드와 둔황: 혜초와 함께 하는 서역기행' special exhibition (18 Dec 2010 - 3 Apr 2011; manuscript on display until 17 Mar 2011 per the BnF's 3-month loan limit): the manuscript's first public display anywhere since Pelliot's 1908 Dunhuang discovery; a second BnF loan followed for the NMK exhibition Dec 2019 - Apr 2020
significance: World-first public display of Korea's oldest travel record of India; made Hyecho's 8th-century India pilgrimage tangible for the Korean public and scholars
evidence: National Museum of Korea archive (2010-06-29); KBS News 2010-12-17; Hani 2019-10-19 (second loan)
